<MethodEndpoint
  method={"get"}
  path={"/api/posts/{postId}/comments"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



For a cross-posted post, the thread is merged across every copy in a
group the caller belongs to, with each comment reported under the
requested `postId` (see `POST /api/posts`). A reply (`parentId`) to a
comment from another copy is stored with that copy's thread.

**Pagination is opt-in** (server feature `paginatedComments`). Send
`take` and/or `cursor` and the response is a `CommentsPage`: the
`take` newest *top-level* comments older than the cursor, each with
every reply under it (at any depth), so a thread never splits across
pages. Items come newest first; reverse them for display and offer
"load older" at the top. Without either parameter the response is the
legacy bare array of the whole thread, oldest first — kept for
already-installed clients. A server without the feature ignores both
parameters and returns that array, so a client can treat a bare array
as one final page.
